title: Walsh characters have degree at most one
statement:
For every subset $S \subseteq [n]$, the Walsh--Fourier character $\chi_S$ has degree at most $1$: every second-order Gowers product of $\chi_S$ equals $1$. Explicitly, for all base points $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ and all direction vectors $h_1, h_2 \in \{0,1\}^n$,
\[
  \chi_S(x)\,\chi_S(x \oplus h_1)\,\chi_S(x \oplus h_2)\,\chi_S(x \oplus h_1 \oplus h_2) \;=\; 1.
\]
replaced: For every $S \subseteq [n]$, the Fourier character $\chi_S$ has degree $\le 1$.
